title: Prepositions of movement
full_content: Prepositions like from, to, into, and toward describe movement direction. Compare “walk into the room” with “walk to the room”.
compressed_content: Use from, to, into, and toward to describe movement direction.
notes: Baseline repeatable card in the active review slot with no queued cards.

title: Prepositions of place
full_content: Use in for containers, on for surfaces, and at for points. “In the box”, “on the table”, and “at the door” each mark a different spatial relationship.
compressed_content: Use in for containers, on for surfaces, and at for points.
notes: Pinned repeatable card. The pin badge is always visible even while the card is active.

title: Adjective order
full_content: Order adjectives by opinion, size, age, shape, color, origin, material, and purpose, as in “a lovely little old round green French silver whittling knife”.
compressed_content: Opinion, size, age, shape, color, origin, material, purpose.
notes: Reviewed card holding the repeatable topic slot while the next occupant is prepared.

title: Conditionals with unless
full_content: Unless means “if not”. “Unless it rains, we will walk” means the walk happens only when it does not rain.
notes: Reviewed card with an empty queue and no hold message; the flow polls for a refill.

title: Phrasal verbs with get
full_content: Get up, get over, and get through change meaning as a unit. “Get over a cold” means recover from it.
